summary.text: 働 is a Japanese-created character meaning “work,” read hataraku in Japanese. Its visible parts suggest a person, 亻, and movement, 動. That association offers a useful way to remember it, but these sources do not document how or when the character was first devised.

history.text: The Chinese-language note concerns a later borrowing of the written Japanese character. It gives a Chinese pronunciation based on 動. That explains the Chinese reading in this record; it does not explain the original Japanese choice of components.

uncertainties.text: The available material identifies 働 as a kokuji, a character created in Japan, but supplies no early Japanese attestations or account of its coinage. The component-based memory aid therefore remains separate from a documented origin story.
